subject: Materials Science
title: Borosilicate Glass: Pyrex and Lab Ware
description: A quick, practical guide to Borosilicate Glass: Pyrex and Lab Ware.

hook.text: Pour boiling water into a regular glass and it cracks. Pyrex laughs at the temperature shock.

buildup.text: Borosilicate glass replaces some soda with boron oxide, drastically lowering thermal expansion.

discovery.text: Low expansion means less stress from temperature changes — the glass resists thermal shock.

twist.text: Corning developed Pyrex in 1915 for railroad lanterns that kept shattering in rain.

climax.text: Lab beakers, telescope mirrors, and oven dishes all rely on borosilicate toughness.

punchline.text: Add boron and glass stops fearing temperature.

quiz.question: Why does borosilicate glass resist thermal shock?
options: It has higher thermal expansion than soda-lime glass
Boron oxide lowers thermal expansion, reducing stress
It is thicker than regular glass
